text:
Statistical Report on 10” Manipur Legislative Assembly Election-2012

INTRODUCTION

General Election to Manipur Legislative Assembly-2012 will go down in the annals
of Manipur as an exemplary and the most elaborate election ever held in Manipur. The
credit for this achievement will surely go to ECI for their unstinted support and timely
advice to the State Election machinery to see that nothing was left to chance. Ministry of
Home Affairs and Ministry of Defense too will share a big chunk of credit for their
contribution for security and air service. State election machinery too may earn some
accolades for implementing the schemes of EC! successfully. The State election
machinery carried out its multifarious responsibilities in conducting General Election-2012
against all odds. Despite some untoward incidents here and there pre-poll and during poll,
completing such a task as this was somewhat an achievement. Election functionaries in
the State can be pleased to themselves that they redeemed the pledge made to the public
and voters in giving them a chance to exercise their franchise once again.

To conduct a single phase election was a no mean task for a small State like
Manipur. Actually, it is not the size that is important, but the gravity of the situation is that
matters. Manipur State has the dubious distinction of reeling under burgeoning insurgency
for many years; it is, therefore small wonder that requirement of security apparatus was
enormous. Induction of 350 companies of CPMFs was the largest ever for Manipur
elections. In addition, more observers were appointed by ECI for General, Expenditure and
Police, altogether 38 officers. This situation entailed greater logistics works in term of
transport, accommodation and coordination. However, State election machinery was able
to carry out all these responsibilities without hitch. Thanks to the Police and Transport
Department for their hard work and dedication.

The Govt. of Manipur deserves unqualified appreciation for rendering all
necessary assistance in term of manpower, maintenance of law and order, security to
candidates, election-related offices and premises, election personnel and EVMs, provision
of transport etc.

One positive thing brought about by announcement of elections was improvement
of POL supply to Manipur. As a result of more than 100-day economic blockade imposed
by Sardar Hill Demand Committee during September-December 2011, the POL supply
came to a near halt and petrol and diesel had to be rationed. These commodities sold
@Rs 180.00 and Rs.100.00 in the black market even after blockade was called off.
However, ECI and State Govt took steps to ensure availability of POL during elections in
consultation with IOC authorities. Dedicated security to |OC convoy on NH 39 (now NH-2)
was provided. Their efforts bore fruit abundantly.

text:
Statistical Report on 10” Manipur Legislative Assembly Election-2012

INTRODUCTION

Implementation of Mode! Code of Conduct cannot be better. No ostentatious
display of money and muscle power was noticed, as a result political campaign was in a
very low key to the satisfaction of general public which was saved from unnecessary noise
and defilement of their properties.

Election Expenditure Monitoring Mechanism was effectively put in place. Income
Tax teams, Flying Squads and Surveillance teams did their jobs admirably. Rs
1,0800000/- was reported seized.

With a view to checking bogus voting and impersonation, an innovative measure
was introduced for taking photographs of all voters inside the polling stations. The
measure was successful in preventing and detecting bogus voting and impersonation.
Based on the findings of the comparison of photographs in the Electoral Rolls with
photographs of voters taken on the date of poll, re-poll was ordered by the Commission in
67 polling stations.

For the first time, facility of voting through Postal Ballot was provided at 16
Designated Camps for UGs under Suspension of Operation (SoO) Agreement with the
Government of Manipur.

Participation of media during elections cannot but be appreciated. Apart from
abstaining from publication of paid news, they rendered total cooperation to the election
department in disseminating information to create public awareness about dos and don'ts
during elections.

State election officials really strained every nerve and burnt the proverbial midnight
oil the next four weeks after poll on 28% January 2012. Our hope for relaxation after poll
was frustrated by a flood of complaints from political parties and candidates. There was no
respite at all till the date of counting. It was rather a miracle that State election machinery
was able to withstand all these odds and hardships.

The confidence reposed by ECI on the State election machinery strengthened our
hands. Despite some incidences which temporarily hampered the election process, we can
say all is well that ends well.

We say a big “Thank You” to all the stakeholders of the Assembly Election-
2012.

POLL PREPAREDNESS

1, ROLL REVISION WITH REFERENCE TO 187 JANUARY 2012: Special Summary Revision of
Electoral Rolls was carried out with reference to 1.1.2012 as the qualifying date. Draft Rolls were
published on 29September 2011 and Final Rolls published on 2 January 2012. The total voters in
Manipur as per the Final Rolls-2012 were 1741518 constituting 63% of the projected population of the
State.

Special thrust was given to registering newly eligible persons in the Electoral Rolls, increasing
PER and EPIC coverage and detecting duplicate and bogus electors.

Electoral Roll Management System (ERMS): ERMS, which was launched in 2011 to enable
public to submit claims for inclusions, deletions, corrections, transpositions and track the status of the
claims was consciously popularized through SVEEP Campaigns during Pre-Revision and Revision
periods. All accepted and rejected forms after disposal by the concerned EROs during the Summary
Revision of Electoral Rolls-2012 uploaded on the website.

Public Grievances Redressal System (PGR): Call Centre with dedicated telephone line
having a toll free number-1950 was opened in CEO office and 11 Public Grievances Cells opened in the
Districts to receive complaints lodged by the public regarding Roll Revision and Conduct of Election.

Statistical Report on 10" Manipur Legislative Assembly Election-2012

POLL PREPAREDNESS

3, GPS MAPPING OF POLLING STATIONS: GPS mapping of all polling stations in the State with
technical inputs from Manipur Remote Sensing and Applications Centre (MARSAC), Imphal was
completed well before the announcement of the Election. This is one of the first of its kind in the country.
This system was of immense convenience as it can pinpoint the location of polling stations, polling areas,
distances, elevations, routes to be taken, etc. It also provided the location of police stations, hospitals,
post offices around the polling stations. It was found very useful especially for the poll parties and security
to advance toward their assigned polling stations.

4. DISTRICT ELECTION PLAN: All District Election Officers prepared District Election Plans well in
advance reflecting district profile, elector details, logistic plan, movement plan, communication plan,
deployment plan, training strategy etc.

5. VULNERABILITY MAPPING AND CATEGORIZATION OF POLLING STATIONS: Identification of

villages/hamlets/habitats and segment of electorate vulnerable to threat, intimidation / interference with
the free exercise of right to vote became all the more necessary in view of the fact that the State has
people from various communities and is having serious law and order problems.

Sector Officers, Returning Officers, District Election Officers and Superintendents of Police did
effective vulnerability mapping and initiated preventive measures.

6. COMMISSION'S VISITS: The full Commission visited Manipur three times -on August 5 2011, from
December 15" to 16 2011 and on January 5 2012 to oversee the poll preparedness. During the
visits the Commission representatives of Political Parties, Election Officials, Police, DEOs and SsP.
These visits sent strong and positive messages to all the stakeholders about the seriousness of the
Commission to conduct free, fair and peaceful election. During its third visit, a meeting was held to
discuss matters which required coordination and cooperation among the neighbouring States in order to
ensure a free and fair election. CSs/ DGPs/ CEOs of Assam, Nagaland and Mizoram, along with CS and
DGP of Manipur were present in the meeting.

7. SYSTEMATIC VOTERS EDUCATION AND ELECTORAL PARTICIPATION (SVEEP) CAMPAIGN:
To motivate voters to participate in the election in large number, as also to woo newly eligible young
people to enroll as voters, a Systematic campaign for voters’ education (SVEEP) was launched on a large
scale. Local TV channel, NCC, NSS, NYKs and Song & Drama division of the State Government were
associated to launch campaign with the fund provided by CEO's office. Brand Ambassadors and Partner
Agencies tremendously helped in motivating the electors and promoting ethical voting. Popular
personalities from film world and sports world were also roped in to organize road-shows and to visit nine
districts spreading the message of participation in voting and honest exercise of franchise.

8. PHOTOGRAPHY OF VOTERS INSIDE THE POLLING STATIONS: Meanwhile, one of the
areas of concern was the alleged incidences of bogus voting in the previous elections. In order to
curb this malpractice the Commission directed use of still cameras to take photographs of all
voters inside the Polling Stations. For this purpose, the Election Deptt of Manipur procured 2621 Lemon
Mobile cameras at a cost of Rs 40 lakhs. This new mechanism was found _ largely effective in that it
discouraged bogus voting and impersonation. Itis therefore little wonder that the State voter turnout
percentage (2012) stood at 79.96% only as compared to 86.37% in 2007 Assembly Election.

POLL PREPAREDNESS

9. WEBCASTING - POLLING STATIONS AND COUNTING CENTRES: To provide transparency and
also to prevent multiple and bogus voting, a system of webcasting was taken up in 60(sixty) highly critical
polling stations on the day of poll. Likewise, counting activities in 14 counting centres also were webcast
on the day of counting.

10. EPENDITURE MONITORING: Elaborate arrangements for training the stake holders on Election
Expenditure Monitoring Mechanism were made at State, District and Sub-District levels. Expenditure
monitoring mechanism was in place with a good number of IRS officers, Income Tax Officials, Flying
Squads, Video Surveillance Teams, Video Viewing Team, Static Surveillance Teams, and Accounting
Teams etc. covering all nine districts and Imphal airport. Control Rooms and Call Centres were set up at
the District Hqs. This tight arrangement to check flow of unaccounted money and illegal transaction of
cash paid off inasmuch as Rs 1,08,0000/- had been seized.

11. With strict implementation of Model Code of Conduct and expenditure, the level of political campaign
was in a low key which created the peaceful atmosphere for the public.

11. Postal Ballot Facility for Cadres of Groups under Suspension of Operation (SoO)
Agreement with the Government of Manipur: For the first time, facility of voting through
Postal Ballot was provided at 16 designated camps for UGs under Suspension of
Operation (SoO) Agreement with the Government of Manipur.

12. SECURITY ARRANGEMENTS: As for security, 350 Companies of Central Armed Paramilitary Forces
and SAFs were inducted to man 2365 polling stations during the elections. In view of the perpetual and
burgeoning insurgency in Manipur and some underground groups campaigning against some political
parties, security needed to be tightened, therefore, induction of massive CAPFs was inevitable.

text:
POLL DAY

DAY OF POLL 28TH JANUARY 2012:

Upon announcement of Election on December 24, 2011, some pre-poll violence, in the form of bomb
plantings and blasts mainly aimed at Congress workers were seen. However, the redeeming feature was
that no organization, underground or over-ground had boycotted the Election. A total no of 279
candidates of various parties were in the fray. Voters started joining the queues from 7AM on 28" January
and voting went on peacefully till 12.30 PM when disturbances were reported in some polling stations
namely Modi and Tampi Chandel district under 41-Chandel AC, At Modi Polling Station, EVMs were
destroyed by some miscreants and at the Tampi Polling station some armed persons (suspect UGs)
entered the polling station by force and killed seven persons including one CRPF, 4 polling officials and
one girl. One suspect UG was also among the dead. This had somehow vitiated otherwise peaceful polls
in the entire State.

disruptions of poll in some Polling Stations were received. Upon being informed, EC! decided that 34
polling stations would have re-polls on 2" February 2012. Re-polls involved 34 Polling Stations in 11 ACs
(out of 19 ACs) in the all five hill districts with 28076 (13788 male and 14288 females) voters on 2™
February 2012. ROs of four valley districts (40 ACs) did not recommend any re-poll. Re-polls passed off
without much ado. However, in some Polling Stations, poll went on till 7.30 PM due to good turn-out of
voters and slow speed of voting reportedly caused by photography of voters inside polling stations.

A plethora of complaints about malpractices still flooded the office of CEO. EC! too received
an avalanche of such complaints and demands for re-polls in a number of polling stations especially in the
hill areas. The Commission directed that photographs of the voters taken on the day of poll/re-poll in
respect of 523 Polling Stations should be checked and compared with the photographs in the Photo
Electoral Rolls in the presence of three Special Observers, Candidates and their agents were also invited
to observe the on-going comparison works. This exercise was taken up on 12!" and 13" of February,
2012. The report thereof was taken by the Observers for further submission to the Commission.

Meanwhile, a new software PICASA IMAGE VIEWER was discovered from Google-2004 which
can compare the photos more accurately. With the PICASA software the task of comparing photographs
of voters taken on the day of poll/ re-poll with the photographs in the Photo Electoral Rolls became easier
and more accurate. The report generated by using Picasa software was hand delivered to the
Commission on 21st February 2012. After seeing the report and recommendation from the DEOs, the
Commission decided on 29" February 2012 to have re-polls in 67 polling stations-one each in Ukhrul and
Churachandpur, 26 in Chandel, 31 in Senapati and 8 in Tamenglong on 4" March 2012 (Sunday).
